{{nihongo|'''Daikai Shrine'''|大海神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Settsu Province]].

'''Daikai Shrine''' (だいかいじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in Sumiyoshi, {{ill|Sumiyoshi-ku, Osaka|Q985702|qid=Q985702}}, {{ill|Osaka|Q35765|qid=Q35765}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} and is currently an auxiliary shrine within the precincts of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|Q705949|qid=Q705949}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
The current enshrined deities are the following two kami{{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Taisha Ryakki|1999|p=25}}:
* {{ill|Watatsumi|Q1474187|qid=Q1474187|lt=Toyotama-hiko-no-Mikoto}} (Toyotama-hiko-no-Mikoto)
* {{ill|Toyotama-hime|lt=Toyotama-hime|Q2329261|qid=Q2329261|qid=Q2329261|lt=Toyotama-hime-no-Mikoto}} (Toyotama-hime-no-Mikoto)

In the *{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}* {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Register of Deities}}, compiled in the 5th year of {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Engi}} ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}), the shrine’s enshrined deities are recorded as two seats{{Sfn|Daikai Shrine Two Seats (Shikinaisha)|1977}}. In the same register, an annotation reads “originally named Tsumori Yasuhito no Kami,” but in *{{ill|Tokusen Jinmyōchō|Q11571092|qid=Q11571092}}* and *{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō Studies|Q11588824|qid=Q11588824}}*, this “Tsumori Yasuhito no Kami” is emended to “Tsumori Ujibito no Kami”{{Sfn|Daikai Shrine Two Seats (Shikinaisha)|1977}}{{Sfn|Daikai Shrine (Deities)|2000}}. Since then, a theory has been known that interprets this shrine as the clan deity of the {{ill|Tsumori clan|Q11555993|qid=Q11555993}} (originally Tsumori no Muraji, later Tsumori no Sukune), the clan that served {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|Q705949|qid=Q705949}}{{Sfn|Daikai Shrine Two Seats (Shikinaisha)|1977}}{{Sfn|Daikai Shrine (Deities)|2000}}{{Sfn|Tsumori clan (ancient clan)|2010}}{{Sfn|Okada Seishi|2011}}. However, in the *{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|Q1045362|qid=Q1045362}}*, Tsumori no Sukune is said to share an ancestor with the {{ill|Owari clan|Q11465311|qid=Q11465311|lt=Owari no Sukune}}, being a descendant of {{ill|Amenohoakari|Q10940411|qid=Q10940411|lt=Hoakari no Mikoto (Ame no Hoakari)}}; this differs from the sea deity (Watatsumi no Kami / Toyotama-hiko), who is the ancestral deity of the {{ill|Azumi people|fr|Peuple Azumi|id|Suku Azumi|it|Azumi (popolo)|ja|阿曇氏|ko|아즈미씨|ru|Адзуми (народ)|simple|Azumi people|qid=Q3377806}}. Another theory identifies the deity described in the *{{ill|Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine Chronicles|ja|住吉大社神代記|qid=Q11381815}}* as “Tsumori Yasuhito no Kami, two offerings, called Sea Deity” with this shrine, and takes the *Engishiki* entry literally as “Tsumori Yasuhito no Kami”{{Sfn|Daikai Shrine Two Seats (Shikinaisha)|1977}}{{Sfn|Daikai Shrine (Deities)|2000}}{{Sfn|Mayumi Tsunetada|2003|pp=152–153}}. Under this interpretation, “Yasuhito no Kami” and “Yasuhito no Kami” are understood to mean an {{ill|Arahitogami|ar|أراشتوجامي|ca|Arahitogami|de|Arahitogami|es|Arahitogami|fa|آراهیتوگامی|fr|Arahitogami|id|Arahitogami|ja|現人神|ko|현인신|mni|ꯑꯔꯍꯤꯇꯣꯒꯃꯤ|pt|Arahitogami|simple|Hitogami|vi|Nhân thần|zh|現人神|qid=Q521834}} or the meaning of {{ill|Arahito Shrine|ja|現人神社|qid=Q85882377}}—the head shrine of the {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|de|Sumiyoshi Sanjin|it|Sumiyoshi Sanjin|ja|住吉三神|mni|ꯁꯨꯃꯤꯌꯣꯁꯤ ꯁꯟꯖꯤꯟ|my|ဆုမိရောရှိနတ်သုံးပါး|pl|Sumiyoshi Sanjin|simple|Sumiyoshi sanjin|zh|住吉三神|qid=Q1114013}} at {{ill|Nakagawa, Fukuoka|ar|ناكاغاوا|arz|بلده ناكاجاوا, اليابان|de|Nakagawa (Fukuoka)|es|Nakagawa (Fukuoka)|fa|ناکاگاوا، فوکوئوکا|fi|Nakagawa (Fukuoka)|fr|Nakagawa (Fukuoka)|hak|Nakagawa, Fukuoka|it|Nakagawa|ja|那珂川市|ko|나카가와시|ms|Nakagawa, Fukuoka|nl|Nakagawa|pl|Nakagawa (Fukuoka)|ro|Nakagawa, Fukuoka|ru|Накагава (Фукуока)|sv|Nakagawa, Fukuoka|tl|Nakagawa, Fukuoka|tr|Nakagawa, Fukuoka|uk|Накаґава (Фукуока)|ur|ناکاگاوا، فوکوکا|zh|那珂川市|zh_classical|那珂川市|qid=Q1206001|lt=Nakahara}}, {{ill|Chikuzen Province|cs|Provincie Čikuzen|de|Provinz Chikuzen|es|Provincia de Chikuzen|fa|ولایت چیکوزن|fr|Chikuzen|gl|Provincia de Chikuzen|id|Provinsi Chikuzen|it|Chikuzen (provincia)|ja|筑前国|ko|지쿠젠국|lt|Čikudzeno žemė|nl|Chikuzen (provincie)|no|Chikuzen (provins)|pt|Província de Chikuzen|ru|Тикудзэн (провинция)|simple|Chikuzen Province|sk|Čikuzen (provincia)|sr|Провинција Чикузен|tr|Chikuzen (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Тікудзен|zh|筑前國|zh_min_nan|Tikuzen-kok|zh_yue|筑前國|qid=Q1047664|lt=Chikuzen}} (the former original shrine of {{ill|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Fukuoka)|abstract|Q29682|de|Sumiyoshi-Schrein (Fukuoka)|fr|Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka)|ja|住吉神社 (福岡市)|simple|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Fukuoka)|zh|住吉神社 (福岡市)|qid=Q29682|lt=Sumiyoshi Shrine}} in Chikuzen){{Sfn|Daikai Shrine Two Seats (Shikinaisha)|1977}}{{Sfn|Daikai Shrine (Deities)|2000}}{{Sfn|Mayumi Tsunetada|2003|pp=152–153}}. In any case, the connection with the Tsumori clan is deep; in the *Sumiyoshi Matsuba Taiki*, it is said that the legitimate son of Tezuri Ashi no Sukune ({{ill|Tamo-mi no Sukune|ja|田裳見宿禰|qid=Q20041346}}, progenitor of the Tsumori clan) served Daikai Shrine as the Great Steward{{Sfn|Daikai Shrine Two Seats (Shikinaisha)|1977}}.

Although the current enshrined deities are the two mentioned above, the *Sumiyoshi Matsuba Taiki* treats Toyotama-hime-no-Mikoto as an associated deity{{Sfn|Daikai Shrine Two Seats (Shikinaisha)|1977}}. As alternative theories, *{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō Studies|Q11588824|qid=Q11588824}}* lists Ōwatatsumi-no-Mikoto and {{ill|Tamayori-hime (mother of Jimmu)|fa|تامایوری-هیمه|fr|Tamayori-bime|ja|タマヨリビメ (日向神話)|mni|ꯇꯃꯌꯣꯔꯤ-ꯍꯤꯃꯦ|pl|Tamayori-bime|ru|Тамаёри-химэ|uk|Тамайорі хіме но мікото|zh|玉依姬|qid=Q3082751|lt=Tamayori-hime-no-Mikoto}} as the two deities, while *Jingi Shiryō* lists three deities: {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shiotsuchi no Oji}}, Toyotama-hime-no-Mikoto, and {{ill|Hoori|Q1051960|qid=Q1051960|lt=Hikohohodemi no Mikoto}}{{Sfn|Daikai Shrine Two Seats (Shikinaisha)|1977}}.

=== History ===
In a document from the first year of {{ill|Daidō|Q1373191|qid=Q1373191|lt=Daidō}} ({{ill|806|Q30021|qid=Q30021}}) contained in the *{{ill|Shinshō Kyakuchokufushō|Q11502312|qid=Q11502312}}*, it is recorded that the then “Sumiyoshi Tarumi Deity” was assigned 22 households as {{ill|Kanbe (social class)|Q11589711|qid=Q11589711|lt=shrine households}}. Of these, two households were assigned from {{ill|Settsu Province|Q864163|qid=Q864163}} by an order dated December 29 of the 3rd year of {{ill|Tenpyō-hōji|Q1346307|qid=Q1346307}} ({{ill|759|Q30532|qid=Q30532}}), and one household from {{ill|Bitchū Province|Q1047514|qid=Q1047514}} by an order dated September 7 of the first year of {{ill|Tenpyō-jingo|Q1373181|qid=Q1373181}} ({{ill|765|Q31216|qid=Q31216}}). There is a theory that identifies this “Sumiyoshi Tarumi Deity” with Daikai Shrine{{Sfn|Daikai Shrine Two Seats (Shikinaisha)|1977}} (another theory identifies it with {{ill|Tarumi Shrine (Q11425829)|Q11425829|qid=Q11425829|lt=Tarumi Shrine}} in Suita City<ref>Eisawa Eitarō, “Tarumi Shrine,” *Shikinaisha Research Report*, Vol. 5, edited by the Shikinaisha Research Association, Kōgakkan University Press, 1977.</ref><ref>*Newly Revised History of Osaka City, Main Text, Vol. 1*, Osaka City, 1988, pp. 41–42.</ref>). Another theory identifies the “two seats of Sea Deities” mentioned in the section on extraordinary festivals in the *Engishiki*, and the “Sumiyoshi Sea Deity” mentioned in the entry for July 5 of the 2nd year of {{ill|948|Q24318|qid=Q24318}} ({{ill|948|Q24318|qid=Q24318}}) in the *{{ill|Nihon Kiryaku|Q1053542|qid=Q1053542}}*, with this shrine, holding that it participated in the {{ill|Yasojima Festival|Q24870749|qid=Q24870749}} together with the Sumiyoshi deities{{Sfn|Daikai Shrine Two Seats (Shikinaisha)|1977}}.

In the *Engishiki* *Jinmyōchō* compiled in the 5th year of {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Engi}} ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}), it is recorded under {{ill|Sumiyoshi district|Q10885872|qid=Q10885872}} of {{ill|Settsu Province|Q864163|qid=Q864163}} as “Daikai Shrine, two seats, minor, originally named Tsumori Yasuhito no Kami,” and the two seats are listed as {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}{{Sfn|Daikai Shrine Two Seats (Shikinaisha)|1977}}.

Thereafter, it continued as an auxiliary shrine of Sumiyoshi Taisha, and it is said that in the past, when the main sanctuary of Sumiyoshi Taisha underwent its periodic reconstruction, the buildings of this shrine were also rebuilt{{Sfn|Daikai Shrine Two Seats (Shikinaisha)|1977}}.

=== Precincts ===
[[File:Daikai-jinja, shaden.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Shrine buildings}}{{small|Heiden on the left, main hall at the back right. A watariden stands between the main hall and the heiden.}}]]
The shrine buildings are located toward the northern side of the Sumiyoshi Taisha precincts. The '''main hall''' dates from the mid-{{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}}, having been constructed in the 5th year of {{ill|Hōei|Q1145262|qid=Q1145262}} ({{ill|1708|Q6846|qid=Q6846}}). Like the main sanctuary of Sumiyoshi Taisha (constructed in the 7th year of {{ill|Bunka|Q1373146|qid=Q1373146|lt=Bunka}} ({{ill|1810|Q6922|qid=Q6922}}), a National Treasure), it is built in the {{ill|Sumiyoshi-zukuri|Q3503635|qid=Q3503635}} style, but it is older than the main sanctuary and, like it, faces west toward the sea. The roof is {{ill|cypress bark roof|Q90373477|qid=Q90373477}}. It is designated as a National Important Cultural Property<ref name="honden"/>.

In front of the main hall stands the '''watariden''' (connecting hall), followed by the '''heiden'''; both were also constructed in the mid-Edo period, in the 5th year of Hōei (1708), like the main hall. The watariden is a two-bay by one-bay structure with double-eaved roofing, covered in hiwadabuki. The heiden is in the wari-haiden style, three bays wide and two bays deep, with a gabled roof, also covered in hiwadabuki. Compared with the main precincts, the construction is simpler{{Sfn|Daikai Shrine Two Seats (Shikinaisha)|1977}}. The watariden and heiden together are designated as a single National Important Cultural Property<ref name="heiden-watariden"/>.

The '''west gate''' standing at the entrance to the precincts in front of the heiden dates from the early Edo period. It is a four-post gate with a gabled roof covered in hon-kawara tiles. It is designated as a National Important Cultural Property<ref name="westgate"/>. Outside the west gate, the terrain forms a cliff, and it is said that the sea once spread out below{{Sfn|Daikai Shrine Two Seats (Shikinaisha)|1977}}. It is also said that there was once a “Taka-haiden” to the southwest of the shrine buildings, but it has now been lost{{Sfn|Daikai Shrine Two Seats (Shikinaisha)|1977}}{{Sfn|Daikai Shrine (Deities)|2000}}.

In addition to the above, there is a well called “Tama-no-i” in front of the shrine, which is said to be the place where Yamasachihiko submerged the tide-jewel he received from the Sea Deity{{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Taisha Ryakki|1999|p=25}}{{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Taisha (Gakuseisha)|2000|pp=204–205}}. Nearby also stands Shiga Shrine, another auxiliary shrine within the precincts of Sumiyoshi Taisha.

=== Cultural properties ===
=== Important Cultural Properties (nationally designated) ===
* Main hall (with attached sacred fence and gate) (structure)
*: Built in the mid-Edo period, in the 5th year of Hōei (1708). Designated on May 26, {{ill|1008 La Paz|Q11540|qid=Q11540}}<ref name="honden">{{National Cultural Properties Database|102|2094|Main Hall of Daikai Shrine, Auxiliary Shrine of Sumiyoshi Taisha}}</ref>.
* Of the Important Cultural Property “Sumiyoshi Taisha, 13 buildings,” the following two structures (structures):
** Heiden and Watariden
**: Built in the mid-Edo period, in the 5th year of Hōei (1708). Designated on December 24, {{ill|TIE fighter|Q19884|qid=Q19884}}<ref name="heiden-watariden">{{National Cultural Properties Database|102|00004494|Heiden and Watariden of Daikai Shrine, Auxiliary Shrine}}</ref>.
** West gate
**: Built in the early Edo period. Designated on December 24, {{ill|TIE fighter|Q19884|qid=Q19884}}<ref name="westgate">{{National Cultural Properties Database|102|00004495|West Gate of Daikai Shrine, Auxiliary Shrine}}</ref>.
